_note: Strum patterns as beat grids. Eight slots to a bar, one per eighth note: 1, 1&, 2, 2&, 3, 3&, 4, 4&. Each slot is "D" for a downstrum, "U" for an upstrum, or null for a slot where the hand keeps moving but does not hit the strings.
_incomplete: PRD §3.2 names three patterns: all downs, then D-D-U-U-D-U, then syncopated. Only the first is here. The other two are not written down yet on purpose — placing D-D-U-U-D-U on the grid takes six strums and eight slots and there is more than one way to do it, and "syncopated" names a family rather than a pattern. Phase 3 builds the strum trainer and adds both from a source, the same rule the chord fingerings followed. One pattern per week (PRD §3.2), so there is a month before this is short.
